title: Recent Progress on Retro-Reflective Metasurfaces and Metasurface Retro-Reflectors
content: Retro-reflective metasurfaces and/or metasurface retro-reflectors have become an active research topic in recent years due to their advantages such as the planar conformal design and versatile scattering control compared to the traditional counterparts. Rely on the generalized Snell's law, a single-layer passive phase gradient meta-surface can realize retro-reflective function but suffers from narrow angular range. By cascading a trans-missive phase gradient metasurface and a reflective one on the back, the combined metasurface retro-reflector can greatly extend the spatial angular range but at the cost of multiple-layer complex configurations, increased device profile and the tedious fabrication processes. Reconfigurable space-time coding metasurfaces with inserted active tuning elements can add the reflective angles towards wide-angle and broadband low-profile metasurface retro-reflectors. This review first gives a brief introduction on traditional all-metal and dielectric-type retro-reflectors which are commonly used in optical, acoustic and microwave domain, and then present recent advancements on metasurfaces-assisted retro-reflectors mainly focused on three types of retro-reflective metasurfaces: single reflective-type, cascaded transmissive-type and active reconfigurable-type. Their design principles, device architectures and the representative performances are summarized. Besides, some key challenges such as wide-angle range, wide bandwidth, high-efficiency, thin device profile, polarization versatile, multi-functional and active tuning are also examined and discussed. By consolidating recent progresses on retro-reflective metasurfaces and metasurface retro-reflectors, this review can provide a comprehensive perspective on this emerging field and also indicating future directions for next-generation ultra-thin, low-cost, wide-angle and broadband planar intelligent retro-reflectors.
